title: Consulting Invoice Template: Hourly, Retainer or Project
description: Bill consulting by hour, retainer or milestone from your browser. No sign-up. PDF, Word, Excel, with BLS wage data, 1099 and estimated tax notes.
lede_html: Bill a consulting job with this form and download a PDF, Word or Excel file. You need no account. The sample is an advisory retainer. Enter your own client and hours.

sample.pay: ACH to Delta Point Advisory LLC
sample.rights: Deliverables transfer to the client on full payment. We keep our methods and templates.
sample.terms: Hours log attached. Travel at cost, no markup.

form.tax_hint: Enter a rate only if your state taxes this service. The form does not decide this.

must_show.heading: What a consulting invoice must show
must_show.intro_html: The invoice links the amount to the agreement: the statement of work, the period and what you delivered. A client finance team often pays against the reference, not the text.
must_show.why_label: Why it matters on advisory work
rows: Ties the bill to an approved budget.
A retainer covers a month, so write the month.
Say which one this bill uses.
Say what the client owns after payment.
A client that files an information return on you asks for your correct taxpayer number on Form W-9.

example.heading: Filled example: milestone project
example.intro_html: A project billed by milestone at sample amounts.

line_items.heading: Consulting work and US wage ranges
line_items.intro_html: Tap Add to put a line on the form. The range comes from the source in the same row, and the button adds a sample inside it. These are wages of employees, not freelance rates. Set your own rate: you also pay your own taxes, insurance and unpaid time.
line_items.after_html: BLS adds that self-employed management analysts are paid by the hour or by the project (BLS).
line_items.range_label: Employee wage range, May 2023 (10th to 90th percentile)

rules.heading: Tax and contract rules for consultants

items.title: How clients report you
items.html: The IRS instructions tell a business to report nonemployee compensation of $2,000 or more on Form 1099-NEC. Your invoices are the record that you check the form against.

items.title: Form W-9
items.html: The IRS says that you give Form W-9 so that the person who files the information return has your correct taxpayer number.

items.title: Estimated tax
items.html: Sole proprietors and others who expect to owe $1,000 or more at filing generally pay estimated tax. A retainer does not hold tax back for you, so set money aside per invoice.

faq.q: Should I bill a retainer in advance?
faq.a: Do what your agreement says. Write the period on the line, for example November advisory, so that the client can book it to the right month.

faq.q: How much detail goes on an hourly bill?
faq.a: Enough for the client to approve it. Show date ranges and topic, or attach a time log and name it in the notes.

faq.q: Do I add expenses with a markup?
faq.a: Follow your agreement. Many consultants bill travel at cost with receipts and say so in the notes.

faq.q: Do I need a separate invoice for each statement of work?
faq.a: It helps the client route the payment. Use one invoice per SOW unless the client asks for one bill per month.
